import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set the style of the visualization

scatter = sns.scatterplot(

    y='price_usd',

    palette='viridis',
    s=100,
    alpha=0.7
)

scatter.set_title('Camera Megapixels vs. Price with Sensor Type and 4K Video Capability', fontsize=14)

# Add a legend with a title

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set the style of the visualization
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between megapixels and price, colored by sensor type
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=data,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    style='has_video_4k',
    palette='viridis',
    s=100,
    alpha=0.7
)

# Set axis labels and title
scatter.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
scatter.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)
scatter.set_title('Camera Megapixels vs. Price with Sensor Type and 4K Video Capability', fontsize=14)

# Add a legend with a title
plt.legend(title='Sensor Type & 4K Video', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
